solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: The lowest point of seabed by Gibraltar …

parts.note: Gibraltar is popularly called the Rock
the seabed is the bottom of the sea

explanation.surface: A diver reaches the deepest spot on the sea floor near Gibraltar, the clue trailing off into the next one.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to 6-across, whose definition carries on the thought; 'by' just joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock bottom is the idiom for the absolute nadir, the lowest level possible.

clue.text: Knock top off ridge and relax

indicators.note: knock top off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a crest is the top of a ridge

explanation.surface: Someone flattens the peak of a ridge and then takes it easy.
explanation.definitionFit: To rest is to relax and stop working.

clue.text: Edged outside to support amusing person warned by police

indicators.note: to support means the second piece goes under the first in this down clue

parts.note: a caution is an informal word for a funny or amusing person

indicators.note: outside means only the outer letters of Edged are used

explanation.surface: A joker who edged along the outside was warned by officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' gives ED from Edged; 'to support' puts it below CAUTION in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cautioned is receiving a formal police warning.

clue.text: Son in period of prosperity gets a welcoming place

indicators.note: in places the son abbreviation inside the other word

parts.note: a boom is an economic period of prosperity

explanation.surface: A son, during good economic times, finds a warm home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts S inside BOOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A bosom is figuratively a warm, loving embrace, as in 'the bosom of the family'.

clue.text: One sticks up for maximum rate at sea

parts.note: top means maximum, as in top speed
a knot is a unit of speed used by ships

explanation.surface: Someone stands up for top speed on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sticks up' sounds like defending, but is literal: hair tied up on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A topknot is a bunch of hair tied on top of the head, so it sticks up.

clue.text: Resisted quiet model in Oxford, ignoring heart

indicators.note: in places the quiet and model pieces inside the trimmed word
ignoring heart means only the first and last letters of Oxford are kept

parts.note: p is piano, the musical term for quiet
to model is to pose

explanation.surface: A quiet model in Oxford was resisted, unmoved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford' tempts as a place name in the surface, but with 'ignoring heart' only its first and last letters serve as the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposed is a synonym of resisted, meaning set against something.

clue.text: … put forward as low point, ultimately

parts.note: to low is to make a cow's sound, moo

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word point

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, someone proposes that the seabed is the lowest place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' looks like an adjective but is the verb for a cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: To moot an idea is to raise or propose it for discussion.

clue.text: City initially offer millions — what a surprise!

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word offer

parts.note: aha is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A city makes an opening offer worth millions, to everyone's astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha is a large city in Nebraska, USA.

clue.text: Give a lift to work, getting rebuke

parts.note: to give someone a lift to a place is to take them to it
a task is a piece of work

explanation.surface: Offering a ride to the office leads to a scolding.
explanation.definitionFit: To take to task is the idiom for to reprimand or criticise.

clue.text: Quid pro quo deal on holiday

parts.note: to deal is to trade
someone off work is on holiday

explanation.surface: A negotiation agreed while away on vacation.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade-off is an exchange where one thing is given for another.

clue.text: Rejects, with no new projections

indicators.note: with no tells us a letter is dropped from the synonym

parts.note: to reject is to spurn, so rejects gives spurns

explanation.surface: Someone turns down offers that come without anything new in them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes N (new) from SPURNS.
explanation.definitionFit: Spurs are pointed projections, such as those on a bird's leg or a mountain ridge.

clue.text: Standard finance should cover exercise book

indicators.note: should cover says the first pieces wrap around the exercise abbreviation

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
PE is physical education, i.e. exercise
to back a venture is to finance it

explanation.surface: Advice that normal funding ought to pay for an exercise book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercise book' reads as one item from school, but exercise is a piece of wordplay and book alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A paperback is a type of book bound in soft card covers.

clue.text: A section of pack ice

explanation.walkthrough: A pack of cards has four suits; 'ice' is slang for gems, so the polar picture is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Diamonds are one suit in a deck of cards and, as gemstones, are called ice in slang.

clue.text: Gave out late shifts by date

indicators.note: shifts suggests the letters of late moving into a new order

explanation.surface: A worker handed out late shifts according to the date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifts' looks like work rotas but is the anagram signal; the date abbreviation goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To deal cards or goods is to hand them out, so dealt means distributed.

clue.text: Advanced voting system goes red, perhaps around the fifth of August

parts.note: PR stands for proportional representation, a voting system

indicators.note: around means the anagram goes about the picked letter
perhaps suggests the letters of goes red could be ordered differently
the fifth of selects the fifth letter of August

explanation.surface: A political system turns left-wing in early August.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges GOES RED; 'around' wraps it about S, the fifth letter of August, giving OGRESSED after PR.
explanation.definitionFit: To have progressed is to have moved forward or advanced.

clue.text: Permit put on phone lock

indicators.note: put on means the second piece is placed after the first in this across clue

parts.note: to phone someone is to ring them
to permit is to let

explanation.surface: Someone is allowed to put a lock on their phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' is a lock of hair, not a security device.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringlet is a curled lock of hair.

clue.text: Much less rent by yourself

parts.note: to rent out a property is to let it
alone means by yourself

explanation.surface: Far cheaper rent if you live on your own.
explanation.definitionFit: Let alone is an idiom meaning not to mention, much less.

clue.text: Person taken advantage of by troubled dominator not at home

indicators.note: troubled suggests the remaining letters being stirred up
not says letters are taken away from the word dominator

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: A downtrodden person suffers under a bully who is never around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not at home' removes IN from DOMINATOR, leaving DOMATOR, which 'troubled' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A doormat is figuratively someone who lets others walk all over them.

clue.text: Circulating current Moslem art is tricky

indicators.note: tricky suggests the letters are juggled into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark that some Islamic art is difficult to interpret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' rearranges MOSLEM ART; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is a powerful whirlpool, a swirling body of water.

clue.text: Shot the wife to share the cost

parts.note: a shot is a go or attempt
Dutch, short for duchess, is Cockney slang for a wife, as in 'my old Dutch'

explanation.surface: A chilling instruction to kill one's spouse to split the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like gunfire but means a turn or try; 'Dutch' for wife is old London (Cockney) slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Going Dutch is the idiom for each person paying their own share.

clue.text: People in tents getting hot instead of cold cramps

indicators.note: hot (H) replaces cold (C), the usual tap abbreviations

parts.note: campers are people staying in tents

explanation.surface: Campers going from chilly to hot get stomach cramps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cramps' is the verb meaning restricts, not muscle pain.
explanation.definitionFit: To hamper someone is to restrict or hinder them, which is what cramps means as a verb.

clue.text: Supporters, of course, eating rotten sweets

indicators.note: eating means the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: on a golf course, tees support the ball
food that has gone off is rotten

explanation.surface: Fans, naturally, are munching on decayed confectionery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' is not 'naturally' but a golf course, where tees hold up the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Toffees are chewy sweets made from boiled sugar and butter.

clue.text: Rebellion of Granite City

indicators.note: rebellion suggests the letters of granite rising up and changing order

explanation.surface: An uprising in Aberdeen, nicknamed the Granite City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Granite City' looks like the nickname for Aberdeen; here Granite is the fodder and City the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangier is a port city in Morocco.

clue.text: Distinguish oneself, getting 40 in spoken Latin

indicators.note: spoken says the letters are said out loud to give a word

parts.note: in Latin (Roman) numerals, 40 is written XL

explanation.surface: A student shines by scoring forty in a Latin oral exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Latin' tells you to write 40 as a Roman numeral; said letter by letter it is ex-el.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to stand out or do exceptionally well.

clue.text: Swear sulphur is part of remedy

indicators.note: is part of puts the sulphur symbol inside the other word

parts.note: a cure is a remedy
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: Someone swears that sulphur is an ingredient in a remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: To curse is to swear or use bad language.

clue.text: Underplay but note one's energy

parts.note: a minim is a musical note, a half note
one is I, and one's is I's, giving I and S
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Someone plays something down, though they note their own energy.
explanation.definitionFit: To minimise is to downplay or treat as less important.

clue.text: Two days lost in Midland city

indicators.note: lost in means those letters drop out of the word Midland

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for day, so two days give two Ds

explanation.surface: A couple of days went missing in a city in the Midlands of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Midland city' reads as one phrase, but Midland is fodder and city the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Milan is a major city in northern Italy.

clue.text: Accept point covered by lawyers

indicators.note: covered by puts the point inside the lawyers' word

parts.note: the Bar is the legal profession, barristers collectively
E is east, a compass point

explanation.surface: Agree to a point raised by the legal team.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something is to tolerate or accept it.

clue.text: Place surrounding unusually green island's national park

indicators.note: surrounding means the first piece goes around the other

parts.note: to place is to set

indicators.note: unusually suggests the letters of green arranged in an odd way

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A location around an oddly green isle belongs to a national park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' signals the anagram of the colour, which the place word wraps around before the island letter ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serengeti in Tanzania is a famous African national park.

clue.text: Substantial part of molecular genetics?

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A question whether something is a significant portion of molecular genetics.
explanation.definitionFit: Large and substantial are synonyms, both meaning big or considerable.

clue.text: Prescribed food that is eaten by dentist with no filling

indicators.note: eaten by puts the abbreviation inside the other piece
with no filling means the dentist loses its middle, keeping only the outer letters

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A dentist recommends a special food regime when no filling is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no filling' leaves D and T from dentist; 'eaten by' puts IE between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A diet is a set regimen of food, often recommended by a doctor.

clue.text: Scientist working more on arts?

indicators.note: working suggests the letters being worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A question whether a scientist is doing more for the humanities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges MORE ON ARTS.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronomer is a scientist who studies stars and planets.
